feed.title: A Box of Tools
feed.subtitle: Free browser tools that never upload your files. Combine images into a PDF or an MP4, compress an image to an exact size, crop a video, or strip EXIF data.

entry.title: Base64 Encoder & Decoder
entry.summary: Encode and decode Base64 in both alphabets, percent-encode URLs, escape HTML entities, and read hex and backslash escapes. It all runs in your browser - nothing is uploaded, so a token never leaves your machine.

entry.title: How to compare two JSON files
entry.summary: Format both files the same way, sort the keys, then diff them. Why a raw JSON diff is mostly noise, how to canonicalise both sides in the browser, and what survives to the patch.

entry.title: How to get phone photos ready for the web
entry.summary: HEIC to JPEG, GPS stripped, resized for the page and compressed to a budget - the whole pipeline in the browser, and the originals never leave your machine.

entry.title: How to make a GIF from part of a video
entry.summary: Cut the seconds that matter first, then convert only those. When the GIF converter's own timeline is enough, when to cut with the video cutter instead, and why every second of GIF costs so much.

entry.title: How to make a boomerang video
entry.summary: Cut the moment, reverse the copy, join the two, and loop it. Three tools in a row, all running in your browser, and the order that keeps the whole job down to a minute.

entry.title: How to scan multiple pages into one small PDF
entry.summary: Photograph every page, get one PDF, combine it with documents you already have, and shrink it until it sends. Three browser tools in a row, and the paperwork never leaves your phone.

entry.title: JSON Formatter
entry.summary: Format and minify JSON, XML, HTML, CSS and YAML, and convert JSON to YAML or XML and back. The parsers run in your browser - nothing is uploaded, so a token or a config file never leaves your machine.

entry.title: Text Diff
entry.summary: Compare two texts and see every difference, line by line and word by word, side by side or in one column. The comparison runs in your browser - nothing is uploaded, so unreleased code never leaves your machine.

entry.title: DICOM Viewer
entry.summary: Open CT, MR, X-ray and ultrasound scans in your browser. Window and level, scroll a whole series, measure in millimetres, read every DICOM tag, and see exactly what in the file identifies the patient. Nothing is uploaded.

entry.title: Document Scanner
entry.summary: Turn a phone photo of a page into a straightened, evenly lit PDF. The corners are found for you, the perspective is undone, the shadow is divided out. Runs entirely in your browser: nothing is uploaded.

entry.title: How to open a DICOM file, and what is in one
entry.summary: What is on a hospital disc, why the files have no extension, how to open a .dcm scan in a browser, what window and level actually does, and what a scan carries about the patient besides the picture.

entry.title: How to redact a PDF so the text is really gone
entry.summary: A black box drawn in a PDF reader usually leaves the words underneath it, and copy-and-paste gets them straight back. What a real redaction removes, the four places a word hides outside the page, and how to check a file before you send it.

entry.title: How to scan a document with your phone
entry.summary: What separates a photograph of a page from a scan of one: the angle, the uneven light, and the file size. How to take the photo, what to fix afterwards, and why none of it needs a server.

entry.title: How to stack photographs to reduce noise, or remove people
entry.summary: Stacking combines a burst of frames into one picture. Which method to use depends on what you are trying to lose: noise, passers-by, or the shallow depth of field on a macro shot. How each one works, what it costs, and how RAW files fit in.

entry.title: Image Stacker
entry.summary: Combine a burst of photographs into one: average them to kill noise, take the median to remove people from a scene, lighten for star trails, or focus stack a macro shot. Reads CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, RAF and CR3 by pulling out the camera's own preview. Runs entirely in your browser.

entry.title: PDF Redactor
entry.summary: Take words out of a PDF instead of drawing a black rectangle over them. The letters are deleted from the page's own drawing instructions, the finished file is opened again and searched to prove they have gone, and nothing is uploaded.

entry.title: ID Photo Maker
entry.summary: Make a passport or visa photo to your country's published rule: exact mm and DPI, a live head-height and eye-line overlay, a background check, a printable 4x6 sheet, and a file squeezed to the portal's KB limit. Nothing is uploaded.

entry.title: Hash & Checksum
entry.summary: Work out the MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 of any file and compare it with the checksum the download page published. The file is read in your browser and never uploaded, at any size.

entry.title: How to check a download against its checksum
entry.summary: How to check an MD5 or SHA-256 checksum on Windows, macOS and Linux or in your browser, what a match actually proves, and the mistake that makes the whole exercise pointless.

entry.title: How to redact an image so the hidden part is really gone
entry.summary: Black boxes drawn in most programs sit on top of the picture and can be moved aside. What separates a real redaction from a covered one, why pixelated text can be read back, and how to check a file before you send it.

entry.title: Image Redactor
entry.summary: Cover a name, an address or an account number in a photo or screenshot and re-encode the picture, so the hidden pixels are gone from the file rather than sitting under a rectangle. Runs entirely in your browser.

entry.title: Password & Passphrase Generator
entry.summary: Make a strong random password, or a diceware passphrase from a bundled 7,776-word list. Drawn by your browser's own cryptographic generator, never sent anywhere, never stored. Free, no sign-up.

entry.title: QR & Barcode Reader
entry.summary: Read a QR code from a photo, a screenshot or your camera, and see exactly where the link goes before you open it. EAN, UPC, Code 128, Code 39 and ITF barcodes too. Nothing is uploaded.

entry.title: Time-Lapse Maker
entry.summary: Turn a long video into a time-lapse: 10x, 60x or any speed you type. Runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded, there is no watermark, and it works offline.

entry.title: GIF Analyzer
entry.summary: Take a GIF apart in your browser: every frame with its delay and disposal, the colour tables, the loop count, and a byte-by-byte breakdown of where the file size went. Nothing is uploaded.

entry.title: How to merge, split and reorder PDF pages
entry.summary: Combine PDFs, cut one into several, and move pages around: what survives the reshuffle, what no tool can carry across, and why none of it needs uploading your documents anywhere.

entry.title: What is actually inside a GIF
entry.summary: Frames, delays, disposal methods and colour tables explained, why browsers refuse the fastest delays, and how to work out where a GIF's file size really went.

entry.title: Audio Trimmer
entry.summary: Play a recording and mark every part worth keeping as it goes past, then save those parts as one file. Sample-exact cuts, no clicks at the joins, nothing uploaded.

entry.title: GIF Splitter
entry.summary: Split an animated GIF into its frames and save each one as a PNG, free and entirely in your browser. Keeps the transparency and the timing. Nothing is uploaded, and it works offline.

entry.title: How to split a GIF into frames
entry.summary: Get every frame of an animated GIF as a PNG: why some frames are only a small patch of the picture, what happens to the transparency, and how to keep the timing so you can put it back together.
